reason: The 'no wall-clock deadline / minutes per step' claim is refuted. agent_runtime._dispatch_tool wraps registry tools in asyncio.wait_for with catalog timeout_seconds=25.0 for web_search (agent_runtime.py:652-666, catalog.py:313), and deep research rounds carry a 90s per-round guard (deep.py:79). The finding's failing-path arithmetic is also off: Lite is tried only after a zero-row success, so a failing DDG turn is 2x2=4 POSTs (plus up to 4 impersonated 403 retries). What survives: DDG's nested budget (up to ~48s of 12s timeouts) exceeds the 25s outer budget. A hanging DDG therefore burns the whole tool budget and wait_for cancels the call before the rotation reaches Brave/Mojeek, so failover never happens.
evidence_checked: code read; ran catalog.timeout_for('web_search') in sidecar venv

reason: Real and self-admitted: pacing.py:31-32 says 'DDG ~3s mirrors the existing ~20/min token bucket in ddg.py', and both throttles run (keyless.py:220, ddg.py:384/391). Mechanism confirmed: record_failure runs on every attempt (keyless.py:227) with ATTEMPTS_PER_ENGINE=2 == DEFAULT_FAIL_THRESHOLD=2, so one fully failed search opens the breaker for 45s. The docstring states this as intended (keyless.py:214-217). Corrected: for DDG each keyless attempt already wraps ddg.py's own 2-attempt loop (ddg.py:60, :212), so benching takes 4+ consecutive failed POSTs, not 'a momentary blip'. The 'blocking engine stays closed' half duplicates finding 3.

Real in code: _impersonated_fallback returns None for any non-2xx including 429 (ddg.py:196-198), and the 403 branch raises SearchError(unreachable) without a reason (ddg.py:225-233). Severity lowered: the mislabel reaches the user only when Brave and Mojeek also fail without any of them rate-limiting (keyless.py:180-198). The keyless error text says 'Wait a moment and retry', not 'no backend configured'. The claim that 403-then-429 is DDG's 'most common hard-block shape' is unverified.
